key_insight: The paper separates exploration from optimization in RLVR by using novelty only in explorer policies, then distilling verified good trajectories into a student trained without novelty pressure.
engineering_relevance: This design lets teams scale exploratory search for new reasoning strategies while reducing the risk that novelty incentives degrade the main model's performance.
method: Train one or more explorer policies with a novelty bonus in the reward.
Filter explorer trajectories for correctness and quality.
Distill the filtered trajectories into a separate student policy and repeat across rounds.
evidence_signal: Across seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two model families, ExpDis outperforms DAPO at the same wall-clock budget and improves pass@k scaling.
watch_item: The approach adds a multi-stage training pipeline with trajectory filtering and repeated alternation, so its practical cost and filter quality are important implementation risks.
paper_title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
